note:
Expert and community consensus, synthesised from FPL analysis sites and the official Scout.

Fields, and why each exists separately:

`case` -- the written argument for picking them.
`watch_out` -- the honest counter-argument, because a recommendation you can't argue against isn't advice.
`key_stats` -- the hard numbers, stored as discrete facts rather than buried in prose so they can be shown next to any decision the app makes about the player.
`voices` -- what named outlets are actually SAYING, attributed. A synthesised paragraph loses who thinks what, and 'analysts say' is not a source. Where two outlets disagree you can see it.
`dissent` -- a genuine split, where reputable analysts argue the opposite of the headline tier. Not the same as a watch_out: a watch-out is a caveat the people recommending the player accept, a dissent is other people saying don't pick him at all. Damps the weighting and releases the must-have lock.

Prices and ownership are as reported at research time and are context only -- the app matches by name and uses live API figures. Club-wide verdicts do NOT belong here; they live in teams.json as machine-readable stances, because advice about a club written into one player's prose reaches one player.

players.name: Haaland
players.verdict: The one genuinely non-negotiable pick, and the consensus captain for GW1.
players.case: The strongest repeating pattern in the game. Haaland has finished as the top-scoring player after the first six gameweeks in all four of his Manchester City seasons, averaging nine goals and 61.3 points across that opening stretch — four from four, not a streak someone is extrapolating from one year. The underlying numbers say the same thing without needing the history: he led the entire league last season in shots per game, big chances per game and xG per game simultaneously, which is not a profile anyone else in the division has. Then the fixture: he opens at home to Bournemouth, a side he has scored against four times in their last four meetings, and City follow with Palace away, promoted Coventry at home, United away and Sunderland at home.
players.watch_out: At 71% ownership he is not a route to rank — he is the baseline everyone else is measured against, and captaining him is the field's default rather than an edge. The real cost is structural: £15.5m is roughly a sixth of the budget, and pairing him with Bruno and Gabriel commits £35.5m to three players, up £6.5m on what the same trio cost a year ago. Everything else has to be built efficiently around that.

players.name: B.Fernandes
players.verdict: The safest premium midfielder, on the best two-gameweek opening in the league.
players.case: The argument is volume from several directions at once. He scored 9 and set up 24 last season — a record FPL assist haul — takes penalties, corners and direct free-kicks, and plays essentially every minute, which is what converts good underlying numbers into weekly returns rather than streaky ones. He crossed the 12-point defensive-contribution threshold in five matches last season too, so even a quiet attacking week has a floor under it. On top of that Manchester United have the best schedule of any side across the opening two gameweeks — Hull away then Ipswich at home, back-to-back against promoted sides — and only one fixture rated above 3 across their opening eight.
players.watch_out: He missed another penalty in pre-season, and Fantasy Football Scout have been flagging the run of misses as a live question over whether he keeps the duty — that matters more than usual for a player whose case leans on dead balls. Separately, £12.0m is the second big commitment after Haaland, and several published drafts deliberately go without him for exactly that reason.

players.name: Gabriel
players.verdict: An official Scout must-have, and the most efficient premium in the game per pound.
players.case: He finished last season on 209 points — the third-highest total any defender has posted in FPL history — and the returns came from every category the game rewards at once. His 18 clean sheets were three more than any other defender. His 30 bonus points were eleven more than any other defender. He added three goals, five assists and 22 defensive-contribution points, and that DefCon figure is the revealing one: it is only eight short of what every other Arsenal defender managed combined. His 6.5 points per game led all defenders. The efficiency argument is the one that actually settles it, though: at £8.0m he returns 0.81 points per game per million, against 0.56 for Bruno Fernandes and 0.44 for Haaland. He is the most expensive defender in the game and still the best value premium in it. With Saliba out, he is also the primary route into an Arsenal defence facing just one top-six side in eight gameweeks.
players.watch_out: The injuries cut both ways. Saliba is out with a back problem and Timber is weeks away with a groin issue, so the back line in front of Raya is weakened exactly when the fixtures look easiest, and the clean sheets may not come as freely as an £8.0m price assumes. There is also a cheaper way to buy the same fixture run: White and Mosquera together cost £11.0m, only £3.0m more than Gabriel alone.

players.name: Raya
players.verdict: Three straight Golden Gloves, and the only defensive asset the template has settled on.
players.case: He has won the Golden Glove in three consecutive seasons, which is about as close to a settled question as goalkeeper gets, and he is behind the defence with the softest opening run in the league. He is also the only defensive player in the game above 30% ownership — the market has made its mind up here while the rest of the defensive picture is still unsettled. Draft analysts make the sharper version of the point: he is the only goalkeeper with a large enough edge over the position to justify paying up at all.
players.watch_out: £6.0m makes him the most expensive goalkeeper in the game, and goalkeeper is the cheapest position to get wrong — the gap between a £6.0m keeper and a £4.5m one is usually a point a week. If Arsenal's defensive injuries bite, you are paying a premium for clean sheets that don't arrive.

players.name: Guehi
players.verdict: The standout mid-price defender on paper — and the most argued-over pick in the template.
players.case: He was the only defender other than Gabriel to finish in the game's overall top ten last season, on 179 points, and the returns came from both ends of the pitch. In the first half of the season at Crystal Palace he produced six attacking returns — two goals, four assists — in 20 matches alongside seven clean sheets, averaging 5.3 points a game. After his move to Manchester City he added another goal, another assist and seven more clean sheets. A defender contributing at both ends is the whole reason the £6.0m bracket works, and he now does it behind one of the best defences in the league.
players.watch_out: Defensive-contribution points reward a style of play, not a player, and moving to a side that dominates possession quietly reduces the amount of defending he actually has to do — the exact mechanism that would undercut his DefCon returns at City. See the dissent below: this is the most contested pick in the current template.

dissent.case: This is a contested pick, not a settled one. RotoWire and Fantasy Football Hub both name him among the highly-owned players to avoid for GW1, and the objection is specific rather than vibes: he has no strong history of defensive contributions, so the DefCon points that make a £6.0m defender work are assumed rather than evidenced; he has not had a full pre-season; and he is 'far from a certainty to start' in a Manchester City side with real depth at centre-back. Their reading is that close to a quarter of the game owns him on reputation rather than on current evidence — the kind of ownership that unwinds inside a fortnight.

players.name: Joao Pedro
players.verdict: An official Scout must-have, and the form player of pre-season by a distance.
players.case: He is the leading goalscorer of any Premier League player across pre-season with seven goals in six appearances — a nine-minute hat-trick in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers, a brace against AC Milan and two more against Real Sociedad. He also arrives fresher than almost anyone in the game, having been left out of the Brazil squad and therefore missing the World Cup entirely, which in an August where England, France, Argentina and Spain players were not back in training until around the 10th-12th is a genuine and short-lived edge. The Scout has him on the official must-have list at £7.5m, and he is expected to lead the Chelsea line.
players.watch_out: Pre-season goals are the softest evidence in football. Analysts have been explicit about the split in his own record: the hat-trick came in nine minutes against Western Sydney Wanderers, a gulf in quality that proves very little, while the brace against AC Milan came against a side actually holding a defensive shape under pressure. Weight the second one and discount the first.

players.name: Szoboszlai
players.verdict: The fourth most-owned player in the game, and the cheapest route into the Liverpool attack.
players.case: He posted 6 goals and 7 assists last season alongside 20 DefCon points and 78 chances created — a chance-creation figure behind only Bruno Fernandes in the entire league. That combination is what makes £7.0m work: an attacking return floor, a defensive-points floor, and set-piece involvement on top. He is nailed for minutes, and with Salah gone there is a live case that penalties come his way too. Ownership has climbed to around 43%, making him the fourth most-owned player in the game.
players.watch_out: He played a deeper midfield role alongside Gravenberch through pre-season, and if that is his job in GW1 the attacking upside people are paying for is not there. Pre-season output was modest at one goal and two assists, which does nothing to settle the question either way. This is a pick whose case rests entirely on a role that has not yet been confirmed.

players.name: Semenyo
players.verdict: Last season's second-best midfielder, at City, priced below the premiums.
players.case: He finished second among all midfielders on 202 points, and does it at £8.5m rather than premium money. Since his £64m move from Bournemouth he is the way to take a share of Manchester City's goals without paying a second premium fee on top of Haaland — the same attack, a much cheaper entry point. The 202-point season is 67 clear of teammate Cherki's 135, which is the cleanest available answer to 'which City midfielder?'. Pre-season has backed it up: five assists in three matches.
players.watch_out: Two caveats, both openly flagged. He ended last season cold, scoring twice in his final nine league games, and minutes are never guaranteed in a City squad with this depth and midweek European football to rotate for. This is the pick in this group most likely to need reviewing after a few weeks.

players.name: Calvert-Lewin
players.verdict: The budget striker that makes a Haaland-led attack affordable.
players.case: At £6.0m he is the enabler that lets the expensive picks coexist. He is nailed, expected to take penalties, and produced 16 attacking returns last season — serious volume for a cheap forward. Pre-season has gone well at three goals and two assists, and analysts point to a specific tactical fit: James Trafford's long distribution behind him suits how he plays. AllAboutFPL project him to score the most points of any £6.0m forward across the opening six gameweeks.
players.watch_out: Stated plainly by the people recommending him: he has a history of troll seasons, and experienced managers own him knowing it could go that way again. He is a means to an end — the money he frees up elsewhere — not a set-and-forget.

players.name: White
players.verdict: The cheap way into Arsenal's defence while the first choices are injured.
players.case: With Saliba and Timber both out, White is set to start at £5.5m, and the published arithmetic is neat: White and Mosquera together cost £11.0m, only £3.0m more than Gabriel on his own. That buys two starting Arsenal defenders on the softest opening run in the league for close to the price of one premium — and Arsenal face just one top-six side across their opening eight.
players.watch_out: He is playing because of injuries, which means his place disappears when they clear. This is a short-term pick with a visible end date, and the end date is not under your control — Timber is described as weeks away rather than months.

players.name: Rice
players.verdict: Over 20% owned on reputation, with no pre-season and a hamstring.
players.case: Nobody is disputing the player. In a normal August he is an obvious Arsenal pick on this run.
players.watch_out: He is back from a deep World Cup run — around 558 minutes — with no pre-season behind him, and has been carrying a hamstring problem. Availability for the opening gameweek is uncertain at best. Carrying a 20%-owned player who might not start is the worst-shaped risk in FPL: you take the downside of the crowd without the upside of a differential.

players.name: Saka
players.verdict: Not a doubt about the player — a doubt about August.
players.case: On form and role he would be an automatic pick in an Arsenal side with this opening run.
players.watch_out: He accumulated heavy World Cup minutes and has been managing an Achilles issue. Even if he starts in GW1, reduced or managed minutes are likely, and at £9.5m there is no room in the price for a player being eased back in. The analysts flagging him are explicit that this is a fitness-timing call rather than a downgrade of the player — he is a buy once he has full minutes behind him.
